doc.title: Jack DeJohnette interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 7, 2025

title: Dance gigs, early rock and roll, doo-wop and playing by ear
summary: He played dances, swing, pop, Fats Domino and doo-wop singing, finding keys and learning parts by ear.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Did you play for dancers on those gigs and did it give you some kind of lesson about tweaking music so people really sort of get into it?

Yeah I mean it was different types of dances going on and things like the cha-cha-cha and certain other things like — actually people played to some swing music too, also, and some pop music also. So yeah generally that worked out pretty good.
And were you playing early rock & roll like Chuck Berry and Little Richard, that kind of thing?
Yeah and what’s the name — Fats Domino. And I also spent a little time in a cappella doo-wop groups too, singing with them.
I read that you had perfect pitch. I wonder if they depended on you for that?
Yeah I mean we’d find the keys till we knew what was right. And also we were covering, you know, get the pitch off the recording.
Uh huh. Everybody learned their parts by ear at that time?
